fact_label: Carte de Séjour pour Inactif documentation shape
value_raw: A Moroccan bank certificate (attestation bancaire) showing sufficient funds, 3-6 months of bank statements, an apostilled clean criminal-record check, a Moroccan medical certificate, and proof of accommodation (lease or title deed). Notably absent: no health-insurance requirement at all — unlike Morocco's student category, which demands a €30,000 medical/repatriation policy. The honest open edge is WHICH financial proof shape a given prefecture actually tests: the sourcing carries both a recurring monthly-income framing (the $1,000-1,650/month cluster) and a one-time lump-sum bank-balance framing (~100,000 MAD shown at application, withdrawable after), with renewal practice reported to test documentation quality hard — cash-only applicants are often refused; clear bank records are what pass.
notes: Extracted 2026-08-07 ([specialist], verdict-coverage review) from the held record only — zero new research. The document list is the route section's own (2026-07-07, [specialist]); the monthly-vs-lump-sum ambiguity is the 2026-07-09 primary-text hunt's genuinely unresolved finding (o-maroc.com 2022 for the 100,000 MAD figure, single-sourced and category-adjacent-corroborated only — the row states it as an open shape question, not a settled number); the renewal documentation-quality pattern is the 2026-07-08 divergence check's adjacent finding. This route's threshold row carries the same no-published-figure honesty — the two rows deliberately tell one consistent story. Informational by design — never a mechanical gate.

fact_label: Remote work on tourist/inactive status — gray-area tolerance and employment-income tax incentive
value_raw: Working remotely for a foreign client/employer while on tourist or inactive-resident status is tolerated in practice (foreign-sourced, foreign-paid income), not an explicit legal right; Moroccan-sourced income earned on tourist status is a clear violation. Tax residents (183+ days/year) are taxed on worldwide income. A 20% flat tax rate (Article 10, Finance Law) applies to certain digital-nomad/expatriate employment income from non-resident employers, but freelance/passive income is reported to fall under a different regime ('Professional Income') and this pass could not confirm how a passive-income source would be classified.
notes: Country-scope fact (applies equally to Marrakech and Taghazout, per our records' own Income viability rows for both locations, which state Taghazout runs on 'the same national tax/visa framework as Marrakech'). CITATION CORRECTED 2026-08-24 ([specialist], [specialist]'s own citation-integrity fix): the previously-cited PwC URL (.../morocco/individual/residence) only supports the 183-day residency test itself, not the 'taxed on worldwide income' consequence — re-fetched directly and confirmed. source_url now points at the correct PwC subpage, .../morocco/individual/taxes-on-personal-income, which states directly: 'Individuals who have their tax residence in Morocco are subject to an IIT on their worldwide income' (re-fetched 2026-08-24). The 183-day mechanism itself remains separately sourced to taxsummaries.pwc.com/morocco/individual/residence (re-confirmed reachable 2026-08-24). The 20% flat-rate incentive (Article 10, Finance Law) is sourced to 9anonai, not PwC — re-fetched and confirmed at https://9anonai.com/en/blog/digital-nomad-tax-morocco-2026 (2026-08-24): 'Article 10 of the Finance Law established a reduced 20% flat tax rate for certain employment incomes of digital nomads and expatriates working for non-resident companies, provided specific conditions are met.' Three claims, two source domains, three URLs — cross-corroborated across independent sources, single source_url field can't hold all three, so the most consequential/quotable claim (worldwide income) gets the field, the other two are cited by full URL here. Extracted 2026-08-23 ([specialist], coverage-matrix gap-fill) from already-written but never criterion-tagged prose.
